summary.text: A 4-month-old boy who could not look up was admitted to find the causes of developmental delay. In the neonatal period he had infectious pneumonia, myocardial damage and hypokalemia that improved with CPAP-assisted ventilation, amoxicillin clavulanate potassium and supportive treatment, and he was discharged. His birth weight was 2.5 kg; the paternal family history showed no abnormality and the maternal history was unknown because the mother was adopted.

Examination at admission showed motor retardation, short stature, a special face with thickened inner canthus, rough facial skin and a slightly thicker tongue coating, with slender fingers, aging skin, ligament laxity and increased hand joint range of motion but normal muscle tension. Ultrasonography showed a patent foramen ovale and left hydrocele testis; x-ray showed spinal deformity, dislocation, slight kyphosis and a widened right hip joint space. Vitamin D was low, while hearing and karyotype were normal.

Gene sequencing found two heterozygous B3GALT6 variants, c.942G>C(p.(W314C)) and c.808G>A(p.(G270S)), verified by Sanger sequencing in the child; the father had the mutant type at c.808G > A and the mother at c.942G > C. No CHST14 mutation site was found. EDS-like SEMDJL1 was confirmed. A hip brace was given and, after treatment, the hip joint was maintained in a good position; follow-up of spinal deformity and facial features continued.
